# SixthSense

Video agent that predicts what happens next on CCTV, verifies it with YOLO boxes, and grades its own predictions against the next clip. Built at the VAST Builders Challenge (London, 17 Oct 2026).

## Stack

- Language: Python 3.12, standard library only in `app/` (the pod has no pip step)
- Framework: none - `http.server` app + one static `index.html`
- Package manager: pip only for optional tooling (`weave`); never required to run
- Database / ORM: VAST VastDB via the VSS backend API (`/api/v1`); results in `app/incidents.json`
- Styling / UI: hand-written CSS in `app/index.html`
- Testing: `python3 pipeline/probe.py` (live API smoke test), `python3 -m py_compile`
- Hosting / CI: team Kubernetes namespace on the VAST lab cluster, Ingress `/app` (`deploy.sh`)

## Commands

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Install | none (optional: `pip install weave`) |
| Dev server | `PORT=8080 python3 app/main.py` |
| Build | none |
| Lint | `python3 -m py_compile app/*.py pipeline/*.py` |
| Format | none |

Before calling a task done, run the compile check and, on the lab VM, `probe.py`.

## Architecture

- Layout: `pipeline/` (watch, verify, foresee, self-check, store), `app/` (web server + page + JSON data), `docs/` (architecture, knowledge)
- Entry points: `pipeline/run.py`, `pipeline/probe.py`, `app/main.py`, `deploy.sh`
- Data flow: VSS search -> YOLO closing-gap check -> Cosmos3-Reason JSON forecast -> LLM judge vs next segment -> `app/incidents.json` -> web app
- External services: VSS backend (JWT), Cosmos3-Reason + YOLO11 GPU endpoints (bearer), W&B serverless inference + Weave
- Copy context: `VOICE.md` (voice, tone, vocabulary, claims policy). All user-facing words follow it
- Hackathon reference repo: `../reference-vast-builders-challenge/` (skills describe every API)
- Deep dives live in `docs/knowledge/`. See its README index; load only what the task needs.

## Conventions

- Read existing code before writing; follow nearby patterns, naming, and structure.
- Keep `app/` flat and stdlib-only: it ships as a Kubernetes ConfigMap (about 1 MiB limit).
- Use relative URLs in `index.html`; the app is served under `/app`.
- Tolerate unknown API shapes with `first()` key lookups; record real shapes from `probe.py` output.
- Only show numbers measured in a real run; label fixture data as fixture.
- Comment *why*, not *what*; match the surrounding comment density.

- Hackathon day: commit straight to `main` in small steps; keep README current for judges.
- Conventional Commits.
- Never commit secrets, `.env*`, clips or probe dumps.

# Code style

- Match the style of the file you are editing before applying any rule below.
- Naming: n/a for this hackathon project
- Exports: n/a for this hackathon project
- Imports: n/a for this hackathon project; order: std/lib → external → internal → relative.
- Functions: small, single-purpose; early returns over nested conditionals.
- Types: n/a for this hackathon project
- Errors: {{throw typed errors | return Result/{data,error} shape}}. Never swallow errors silently.
- Constants and config live in `pipeline/modes.py`. No magic numbers or strings inline.
- Comments explain *why*. Delete commented-out code.
- Formatting is owned by no formatter (match the file). Don't hand-format; the PostToolUse hook runs it.

# Context hygiene

- One fact per bullet, imperative, ≤30 words. No stories or dates in hot files.
- Don't write what the code already says (commands, structure); it is injected at session start.
- Never hand-edit generated adapters (listed in AGENTS.md); after editing any context file, run `ctx.py sync` and `ctx.py registry` before committing, or CI's `ctx.py check` fails.
- When the context linter reports a violation, fix it before continuing.

# Git

- Branch names: `n/a for this hackathon project/<short-slug>`. Never commit straight to `main`.
- Commits: Conventional Commits, imperative subject ≤ 72 chars, body explains *why*.
- One logical change per commit. Don't mix refactors with behavior changes.
- Before committing: lint, type-check, and the relevant tests pass.
- Never: force-push shared branches, rewrite published history, commit `.env*` or build output.
- PRs: use `/review` first; the description covers what, why, how it was tested, and screenshots for UI.

# Security

- Never read, print, log, or commit secrets. Use env vars; reference `.env.example` for names only.
- Validate and parse all external input at the boundary (plain type checks at the HTTP boundary).
- Parameterized queries only. No string-built SQL, shell, or HTML.
- AuthN/AuthZ checks go on the server, on every protected route/action. Never trust the client.
- Escape output by default. No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` / `eval` / `exec` with user data.
- New dependency → check maintenance, license, and known CVEs; ask before adding.
- Least privilege for tokens, DB roles, and cloud IAM.
- When in doubt, stop and flag it to the user instead of guessing.
